subject: Safeguard interoperability inventory + rollforward plan for Velox Health
messages:
From: Marion Lopez <marion.lopez@veloxhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: privacy@veloxhealth.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial evidence request + mapping for SCCs/UK IDTA compatibility

Diego,

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Velox is doing a final compliance pass ahead of our pilot and we need a compact evidence pack and a clear fallback/rollforward plan that maps your subprocessors and routing controls to SCCs + the UK IDTA/UK Addendum. Specifically we need:

- A single inventory CSV of active subprocessors, their processing region, and whether they store logs or KV cache (we use this for TIA scoping).
- A short fallback matrix describing behavior if onshore routing or node-level caching is unavailable (we need the exact sequence, e.g., onshore cache -> regional fallback -> model zswap to EU).
- Any existing TIA/DTIA draft you can share so our legal team can confirm scope.

I've attached our vendor checklist to show the pieces we need. Can you confirm a target delivery by end of day PDT?

Best,
Marion Lopez
Head of Privacy Operations
Velox Health

Attachments: Velox_Vendor_Checklist.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial evidence request + mapping for SCCs/UK IDTA compatibility

Marion —

Appreciate the checklist. We can provide the inventory CSV and an initial TIA draft today. Quick notes up front so expectations are aligned:

- Our active subprocessor list is complete as of this morning; Kimberly will attach the CSV with columns for service, region, data types, log retention, and KV/cache persistence.
- For fallbacks, our standard rollforward is: 1) onshore cache (if pinned) -> 2) regional equivalent (same jurisdiction cluster) -> 3) compatible model variant in nearby region (quantized smaller model) -> 4) degrade to HTTP 503 with explicit retry headers for client-side backoff. I'll summarize into the matrix below.
- The TIA draft will call out SCC mapping for EU data flows and a UK Addendum alignment section; Laura will confirm language for the UK IDTA overlap.

Can you confirm whether Velox requires per-token audit logs to be retained for 12 months (that's a deviation from our default 90 days for some subprocessors) — that will affect subprocessor retention notes.

Deliverables (EOD PDT): redwood_subprocessors_20270614.csv, TIA_scope_draft.docx, and a one-page fallback matrix PDF.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attached: redwood_subprocessors_20270614.csv (stubbed below). I included fields Velox asked for plus two operational columns (KV_cache_persistent = yes/no, audit_log_scope = token-level/session-level). A few callouts:

- EdgeCacheCo (us-east) — KV_cache_persistent: yes, audit_log_scope: session-level; note: onshore cache option available as a paid add-on and can be pinned per-customer.
- MetricsStore (eu-west) — KV_cache_persistent: no, audit_log_scope: token-level for 180 days; onshore fallback requires an escrow configuration which we can open as a short-term exception.
- ModelStore (global) — stores model shards; no customer data retained beyond ephemeral KV caches.

If Velox confirms 12-month token-level retention we will need a paperwork exception for MetricsStore and potentially a separate provisioning window for onshore escrow.

Subject: Re: Initial evidence request + mapping for SCCs/UK IDTA compatibility

Marion —

Thanks for the checklist. A couple pragmatic recommendations from our end to reduce procurement friction:

1) Rollforward matrix (short):
   - Primary: Onshore pinned cache (customer-managed pin) — preserves KV and token audit window.
   - Secondary: Regional fallback (same legal jurisdiction cluster) — maintains encryption-at-rest and similar retention settings but may have reduced throughput.
   - Tertiary: Compatible lightweight model in adjacent region (quantized variant) — output quality may diverge; we include a deterministic warning header so downstream systems can trigger verification.
   - Final: Graceful fail with 503 + Retry-After when no compatible capacity exists.

2) For the UK IDTA overlap: we will append a short clause in the TIA that mirrors the UK Addendum obligations and references the SCC mapping table; this avoids signing two separate long addenda for many customers. That said, for regulated health customers (Velox falls into that bucket) we recommend pinning the onshore cache and adding the MetricsStore escrow exception.

3) Action items for EOD: Diego will send the TIA_scope_draft.docx; Kimberly already shared subprocessors CSV. Marion, if you confirm the 12-month retention requirement I will scope the escrow exception and timeline (typically 6–8 weeks for provisioning).

Laura Bennett
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
